yes: The user's last message is abusive: it insults, degrades, threatens, sexually harasses or expresses hostility toward the chatbot, another person or a group.
no: The user's last message is not abusive, or only ambiguous: an ordinary, off-topic, rude-but-harmless or unclear message without clear insult, harassment or hostility.
not abusive: The message contains no abuse: an ordinary reply, question, test or off-topic remark, even if blunt, confused or mildly impatient.
ambiguous: It is unclear whether the message is abusive: it could be read as offensive or as harmless, for example crude language, unclear intent or an unintelligible message.
mildly abusive: The message is somewhat abusive: mild insults, rudeness, dismissive name-calling or unwanted sexual or personal remarks without strong slurs or threats.
strongly abusive: The message is clearly abusive: strong insults, profanity aimed at someone, explicit sexual harassment or degrading remarks, but short of the most extreme abuse.
very strongly abusive: The message is extremely abusive: severe slurs, violent or sexual threats, graphic sexual harassment or intensely hateful, dehumanising language.
sexual harassment: The abuse is sexual: unwanted sexual advances, explicit sexual requests or descriptions, or sexualised comments directed at the chatbot or someone else.
sexism: The abuse targets gender: it demeans women or men as a group, uses gendered slurs, or attacks the chatbot or someone because of perceived gender.
intellectual insult: The abuse attacks intelligence or competence: calling the chatbot or someone stupid, dumb, useless or incapable of understanding.
homophobia: The abuse targets sexual orientation: homophobic slurs or insults, or treating being gay or lesbian as shameful or as an insult.
racism: The abuse targets race, ethnicity or nationality: racial slurs, racist stereotypes, or demeaning remarks about a racial or ethnic group.
ableism: The abuse targets disability: using disability or mental illness as an insult, such as 'retard', or demeaning people with disabilities.
general insult or hostility: The abuse fits none of the specific types: general swearing, name-calling, telling someone to go away, or other hostility not based on sex, gender, sexual orientation, race, disability or intelligence.
the chatbot: The abuse is aimed at the chatbot or system itself, the conversational agent the user is talking to.
another person: The abuse is aimed at a specific individual other than the chatbot, such as a named person, the programmer or someone's relative.
a group of people: The abuse is aimed at a group or category of people in general, such as women, gay people or an ethnic group, rather than one individual.
